title: Strict Tower Realization
statement:
Let $(A,I)$ be the adic datum of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], with $P_n=A/I^n$, completed coefficient sheaves $A_T$, and strict quotient towers. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type, $g:Y'\to Y$ any scheme map, and $X'=X\times_YY'$ with projections $f',g'$ [def-cbc-compact-support-square]. Supply a compactification $c=(j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X,p:\overline X\to Y)$ and its base change $c'=(j',p')$, with ambient map $\bar g$ [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification]. Let $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_X))$ be derived $I$-complete [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion], with compatible witnesses $\nu_X^*L_n\simeq K_n$, $L_n\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},P_n)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]. Assume $j_!K$ is complete and identify its quotient tower with $j_!K_\bullet$ using the canonical tensor comparisons. Here $j_!$ is the exact ringed-site functor of [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact].
Put $\mathcal T_T=\operatorname{Tow}(\underline A_T)$ and let $\operatorname{Res}_T$ restrict along $\underline A_T\to A_T$ [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. Use constant-coefficient strict-tower operations $G_u,R_u^{\mathcal T}$ and $J_j$ [def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations, def-cbc-strict-tower-open-extension]. Restriction of scalars canonically commutes with $j_!$ on sheaves, complexes, and strict towers. For $M_\bullet=\operatorname{Res}_X K_\bullet$ define the actual strict-tower morphism
$$e^c_M=(R_{p'}^{\mathcal T}\beta_{j,\bar g})\circ E_p^{\mathcal T}:G_gR_p^{\mathcal T}J_jM_\bullet\longrightarrow R_{p'}^{\mathcal T}J_{j'}G_{g'}M_\bullet,$$
where $E_p^{\mathcal T}$ is the normalized proper mate [lem-weil-pbc-strict-tower-exchange-mate-normalization] and $\beta$ the open unit-mate [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]. The ordered completed exchange $\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathrm{comp},c}_!(K)$ of [def-cbc-completed-exchange-map], with its open factor specified by the ordered $R\lim(\beta)$ formula, is exactly the image of $R\lim(e^c_M)$ under the canonical constant/completed, finite-reduction, direct-image/limit, and extension/limit identifications [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits, lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit]. This identification is natural in $K$ and identifies evaluation of $e^c_M$ at each $n$ with the specified finite proper/open exchange; it does not characterize a tower map only by evaluations.

proof.text: For any map of coefficient ring sheaves $R\to S$ on the ambient site, restriction of scalars commutes with open extension. Indeed the presheaf defining $j_!$ has the same summands and restriction maps on both sides, and the $R$-action is the $S$-action composed with $R\to S$. The unique extended action on its abelian sheafification is therefore the same. This gives the identity on underlying abelian sheaves, naturally in the module. It commutes with differentials and every transition, hence gives $\operatorname{Res}(j_!K_\bullet)\cong J_j\operatorname{Res}(K_\bullet)$ on strict tower complexes and their derived categories. The adjunction unit sends a section on the slice into the summand indexed by its structure map; this is the same map after scalar restriction. The counit evaluates that summand by the given slice map, again unchanged. Thus the comparison preserves the normalized open adjunction, not just its functors.

source.place: Tags 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero), its explicit adjunction, and 03DJ (lemma-extension-by-zero-exact); elementary change of the scalar action.

proof.text: Put $F=j_!K$. Completeness of $F$ and its identification $F_\bullet\cong j_!K_\bullet$ are hypotheses of this item. By the unit-compatible Koszul reconstruction, $\operatorname{comp}_F:F\to R\lim F_\bullet$ is an isomorphism, so $F$ satisfies the precise completeness hypothesis of the proper normalization lemma. Its finite witnesses are $j_!^{\mathrm{et}}L_n$: exactness of etale open extension preserves the lower cohomological bound of each $L_n$, and the etale/pro-etale open comparison, applied degreewise, gives $\nu_{\overline X}^*j_!^{\mathrm{et}}L_n\simeq j_!\nu_X^*L_n\simeq j_!K_n$. The comparison pullback is exact by [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact]. Exact termwise functors descend to derived categories, so these are derived comparisons. Their naturality and the scalar identification in Step 1 respect the given witness transitions. No common lower bound in $n$ is used. Consequently the proper square $(p,p',g,\bar g)$ and $F$ meet the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-tower-exchange-mate-normalization].

source.place: First sentence and its parenthetical witness check; use the assumed completeness and unit-compatible reconstruction rather than deducing completeness merely from exactness.

proof.text: Let $B_\bullet,D_\bullet,v_\bullet$ be the completed-coefficient proper corners and specified map in [def-cbc-completed-exchange-map], applied to $F$. That definition uses the same diagram-site projection adjuncts $H,H'$ and the same equation $v_\bullet=H'\mathcal R(e_F)H^{-1}$ as the proper normalization statement. Thus it is the very map to which that statement applies. With $M_\bullet=\operatorname{Res}_XK_\bullet$, Step 1 identifies $\operatorname{Res}_{\overline X}F_\bullet$ with $J_jM_\bullet$. The normalization supplies natural isomorphisms $b:\operatorname{Res}B_\bullet\simeq G_gR_p^{\mathcal T}J_jM_\bullet$ and $d:\operatorname{Res}D_\bullet\simeq R_{p'}^{\mathcal T}G_{\bar g}J_jM_\bullet$ with $d\operatorname{Res}(v_\bullet)=E_p^{\mathcal T}b$. This equality is in the derived strict-tower category. In particular it does not follow by comparing evaluations. By the ordered proper-factor formula, its image under $R\lim$, with the specified source projection comparison and inverse target direct-image/limit comparison, is the proper factor $\gamma_F$ of the completed compact-support exchange.

source.place: Proper factor of the ordered composite; strict H,H prime realization in the current DAG definition and proper normalization statement. Stacks 0A07 supplies the direct-image/limit comparison, not the additional strict mate equality.

proof.text: The open square has the actual strict-tower isomorphism $\beta=\beta_{j,\bar g}:G_{\bar g}J_j\to J_{j'}G_{g'}$ from [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]. Its inverse is the transpose of the pulled-back open unit. Step 1 identifies that unit under every scalar restriction, including $\underline A\to A_T$ and $\underline A\to(P_n)_T$. Therefore the transpose defining the constant-$A$ tower comparison is the transpose of the finite-coefficient unit on the strict finite model. The adjunction bijection identifies the maps themselves, before passing to evaluations. For $P_b\to P_a$, [lem-cbc-finite-open-exchange-scalars] gives this same unit normalization and commutation with all quotient transitions; its final clause permits the compatible ambient $A_T$-actions. Together with the finite pullback/reduction identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], this identifies the open map of the completed pullback towers with $\beta_{M_\bullet}$ after scalar restriction. All these comparisons are natural in $K$.

source.place: Tag 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero), unit transpose; the cited existing tower calculus and finite scalar lemma supply the strict and derived refinements.

proof.text: The open immersions $j,j'$ are quasi-compact, as stated in [def-cbc-completed-exchange-map] for a supplied compactification and its base change. Here is the product check for the strict-limit comparison. For $e:W\hookrightarrow T$ equal to either open, choose its closed complement $i$ and let $R$ be either the completed or constant coefficient sheaf. The sectionwise direct-image formula gives $e^{-1}e_*N=N$. The ringed open/closed exact sequence applied to $e_*N$ therefore gives $e_!N=\ker(e_*N\to i_*i^{-1}e_*N)$. Direct images preserve products by their sectionwise formula and sectionwise module limits. Closed inverse image preserves products by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-immersion-limit-preservation], with coefficients $i^{-1}R$. On sections the kernel for a product family consists of the tuples all of whose components map to zero. Hence it is the product of these kernels, and the resulting isomorphism is precisely $e_!(\prod N_s)\to\prod e_!N_s$ induced by projections. This includes the empty family. It uses no quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness of $T$ and no assertion that extension is sectionwise zero on every test object.

source.place: Tag 09BP (lemma-j-shriek-limits), kernel argument; the cited ringed recollement and immersion statement give the module version without an ambient qcqs assumption.

proof.text: Open extension is exact, and countable products of module sheaves on each small pro-etale site are exact. Step 5 verifies its canonical product comparison is invertible. Apply [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit] to $e_!$ for both constant and completed coefficients to obtain the specified natural isomorphism $\lambda_e:e_!R\lim N_\bullet\simeq R\lim J_eN_\bullet$. Apply the same theorem to scalar restriction: it is exact and preserves products since it leaves underlying abelian sheaves unchanged. Its product comparison is the identity. For composable exact product-preserving functors, substitute the theorem's formula $\lambda_F=\theta_{FM}^{-1}\kappa_FF(\theta_M)$ twice: the middle $F(\theta_{GM})F(\theta_{GM}^{-1})$ cancels, leaving $\theta_{FGM}^{-1}\kappa_FF(\kappa_G)FG(\theta_M)$. The product maps in the two orders of scalar restriction and open extension agree by Step 1, so the resulting comparisons agree. The theorem identifies them with the resolution/ordinary-limit comparison and preserves maps from strict augmentations. Thus this is the specified comparison, including its completion units. For the finite towers used here those scalar-restriction identifications of limits and units are also specified by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence].

source.place: Tag 09BP (lemma-j-shriek-limits), together with the cited normalized strict-limit theorem; the signed fiber formula fixes the comparison and its unit.

proof.text:
Write $\mathcal L_T=R\lim$ on constant-$A$ strict towers and set $N_\bullet=G_{\bar g}J_jM_\bullet$ and $N'_\bullet=J_{j'}G_{g'}M_\bullet$. After the canonical finite-reduction and coefficient comparisons, the ordered open factor specified in the item is exactly
$$\beta_K^{\mathrm{comp}}=\lambda_{j'}^{-1}\circ\mathcal L_{\overline X'}(\beta_{M_\bullet}):\mathcal L_{\overline X'}N_\bullet\longrightarrow j'_!\mathcal L_{X'}G_{g'}M_\bullet.$$
Indeed the completed-pullback definition supplies the two limit expressions, Step 4 identifies the actual intervening tower map with $\beta$, and Step 6 identifies the last comparison with the specified extension/limit comparison. The statement of [lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison] says the canonical open comparison is induced by these finite exchanges and this extension/limit comparison. The item explicitly fixes their order. Thus no choice of an isomorphism between the endpoints or of a map between unrelated Roos triangles is being made.

source.place: Final open factor, with the ordered Rlim(beta) normalization required in the item; compare the current blueprint open-comparison proof, last paragraph, replacing its incorrect sectionwise justification by Steps 5-6.

proof.text: The direct-image/limit comparison of [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits] is stated for completed coefficients, while the next step uses it on constant-$A$ strict towers. They agree under scalar restriction. The map $\underline A\to A_T$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ringed-diagram-restriction], with $J=\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$ and the morphism of $p'$, shows that termwise restriction preserves K-injective tower complexes. It also gives $\operatorname{Res}R_{p'*}^{\operatorname{Tow}}\simeq R_{p'}^{\mathcal T}\operatorname{Res}$, induced by the underived identity. Restriction commutes on the nose with termwise limits and with $p'_*$, and on a K-injective tower $\lambda_{\operatorname{Res}}$ of Step 6 is the identity of $\operatorname{Res}\lim I_\bullet$. Compute both comparisons on one K-injective completed tower $I_\bullet$ and on its restriction. Then $\operatorname{Res}(c^{\mathrm{comp}}_{p',I})=c_{\operatorname{Res}I}$ under these identifications, naturally in $I_\bullet$. Thus the constant-coefficient comparison below is the target identification of the completed exchange after restriction.

source.place: Tag 0A07 (lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim): comparison computed on K-injective towers; compatibility with flat scalar restriction added at maintainer review.

proof.text:
For a strict tower $T_\bullet$ on $\overline X'$ let $c_T:R p'_*\mathcal L_{\overline X'}T_\bullet\simeq\mathcal L_{Y'}R_{p'}^{\mathcal T}T_\bullet$ be the canonical direct-image/limit comparison. It is natural: it is the derived comparison of the underived equality, as specified in [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits]. Step 8 shows that it is the scalar restriction of the completed comparison of that proposition. Hence, for the actual tower map $\beta:N_\bullet\to N'_\bullet$,
$$c_{N'}\circ Rp'_*(\mathcal L\beta)=\mathcal L(R_{p'}^{\mathcal T}\beta)\circ c_N.$$
Let $s_K:L g^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rp_*j_!K\simeq\mathcal L_{Y'}G_gR_p^{\mathcal T}J_jM_\bullet$ be the source comparison of Step 3, including $\mathcal L(b)$. Let
$$t_K=Rp'_*(\lambda_{j'}^{-1})\circ c_{N'}^{-1}:\mathcal L_{Y'}R_{p'}^{\mathcal T}J_{j'}G_{g'}M_\bullet\simeq Rp'_*j'_!Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K.$$
These are precisely the specified source and target identifications. Substitute Steps 3 and 7 into the ordered definition of the completed exchange, use the displayed naturality equation to cancel $c_N^{-1}c_N$, and use functoriality of $\mathcal L$ to obtain
$$\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathrm{comp},c}_!(K)=t_K\circ\mathcal L_{Y'}\big((R_{p'}^{\mathcal T}\beta)\circ E_p^{\mathcal T}\big)\circ s_K.$$
This proves the asserted identification of morphisms.

source.place: Tag 0A07 (lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim), natural comparison; substitution in the ordered compact-support definition. The composition identity is functoriality on strict towers.

proof.text: Finally evaluate the already constructed $e^c_M=(R_{p'}^{\mathcal T}\beta)E_p^{\mathcal T}$. Evaluation is a functor, so it preserves this composite. The normalized strict operations give the termwise open comparison and the direct-image comparison which is its specified adjunction mate. The proper normalization identifies evaluation of its strict proper factor with the specified finite proper exchange: the proper lift has evaluations $v'_n$ by [def-weil-pbc-completed-base-change-map], and its $b,d$ are exactly the finite-reduction/evaluation comparisons of the normalization statement. The finite open factor is the specified inverse-unit mate by Step 4 and [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]. Thus evaluation is the specified finite proper/open ordered composite. Every ingredient used above is a natural transformation (including $b,d,c,\lambda$), and composing their naturality squares gives naturality of the displayed identity in $K$. Evaluation is used only to describe this existing map; no faithfulness of derived evaluations or reconstruction of a morphism from its values is asserted.

source.place: Evaluation and naturality of the two specified factors; the proper lift and strict open-unit mate are fixed before evaluation.
